subject: Short-run pilot: voucher vs usage ceiling — NeuroNova ask
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@neuronova.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@neuronova.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Short-run pilot — options we discussed

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We need one final ask from Redwood: the pilot is wrapping up next week but our product team wants 3–4 more weeks of traffic to validate the integration. Procurement will only approve a single amendment, so we'd like a concise menu of options you can sign off on quickly.

Specifically, we are deciding between two approaches and want your price/term tradeoffs:
- a one-time voucher (prepaid token bucket) we can consume over the extension period; or
- a short duration SKU (time-boxed extension) with a hard usage ceiling and prorated pricing.

Key constraints:
- We need predictable unit costs for finance;
- We need a soft concurrency guarantee (we're okay if it’s not an SLA but need guidance on headroom);
- Procurement needs an invoiceable item and a concise statement of work or amendment to sign.

I attached our usage summary for the pilot so you can size options (NeuroNova_usage_summary.csv). Can you circle back with a recommended path + a short sample term sheet we can present to procurement?

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Product
NeuroNova Therapeutics
[attachment: NeuroNova_usage_summary.csv (text/csv, 18 KB)]
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@neuronova.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run pilot — options we discussed

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear note and for the usage file. Forwarding to Ben and Monica to capture both commercial and implementation constraints.

Quick summary of two pragmatic options we typically offer:

1) Voucher (prepaid token bucket) — recommended when you want zero surprises
   - One-time voucher of tokens usable over the extension window
   - Can be set to expire at the end of the extension (no ongoing commitment)
   - Conversion credit for committed T&Cs if you convert to Dedicated within 90 days
   - Pros: simplest for procurement, predictable unit pricing; Cons: upfront payment

2) Time-boxed SKU (prorated extension with usage ceiling)
   - Flat fee covers the extension window up to an agreed token ceiling
   - We can add a small overage rate if you exceed the ceiling
   - Pros: no upfront voucher accounting; Cons: requires precise ceiling estimate, possible overage

From a concurrency/headroom perspective we can offer a soft capacity buffer (reserved baseline + burst pool) for the extension — not a firm SLA but operationally we set routing preferences to avoid throttling for pilot traffic. Monica can speak to the implementation details.

Ben — can you draft the two-term samples (voucher and time-boxed SKU) and include an option for a 3-week vs 4-week extension so Samir can present to procurement?

Samir — we’ll attach short one-page term samples and a lightweight amendment that procurement can sign (invoice-friendly language). Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: samir.kapoor@neuronova.com
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run pilot — options we discussed

Samir — attaching two short term docs: a voucher term sheet and a time-boxed amendment. High level commercial offer below.

Offer A — Short-run voucher (clean procurement path)
- Voucher size: 150,000 tokens (covers current run rate + 25% buffer based on usage.csv)
- Price: $0.80 per 1k tokens (one-time charge = $120) — includes 10% pilot discount
- Validity: voucher valid for 28 days from activation; no ongoing commitment
- Conversion: if you convert to an annual commitment within 60 days, voucher value applied as a credit at 120% (to accelerate conversion)
- Attachment: short_run_voucher_terms.pdf [attachment stub]

Offer B — Time-boxed extension (invoice line item)
- Duration options: 21 days or 28 days
- Ceiling: 135,000 tokens (21d) / 180,000 tokens (28d)
- Price: prorated seat + capacity bundle; 28-day example = $145 (invoice line)
- Overage: $1.10 per 1k tokens after ceiling

Operational note: for either option we can enable a temporary burst pool (soft concurrency reserve) for the extension window; we’ll document routing rules and a simple runbook for your SREs.

Request: can you confirm preferred option and any procurement constraints by EOD Apr 8 so we can issue a single amendment?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: short_run_voucher_terms.pdf (application/pdf, 24 KB)]
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@neuronova.com>
To: ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@neuronova.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run pilot — options we discussed

Thanks Ben and team — quick internal note after a sync with procurement and engineering:

- Procurement prefers Offer A (voucher) because it’s easy to invoice and recognizes as prepaid consumption.
- Engineering wants the voucher to include a minimum soft concurrency guarantee: specifically, sustained 6 concurrent streams with 20 concurrent burst capacity for short spikes; they understand this is not a full SLA but need the guarantee documented.
- Procurement also asked if you can split the voucher into two invoice line items (voucher + implementation credit) so they can route the PO.
- One ask: can the voucher be 28 days but we’d like a 4-week calendar window (so effectively 28–30 days depending on start) — procurement wants a date range on the amendment.

If you can accommodate the concurrency buffer and split invoice lines, we can sign quickly. Also cc’ing Leah (procurement) to weigh in on invoice wording.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Samir
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@neuronova.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@neuronova.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run pilot — options we discussed

Samir / Leah — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise compromise we can put into a single amendment and turn around via DocuSign. I’ll attach a one-page POC voucher agreement you can share with procurement.

Final proposal (compromise):
- Voucher: 150,000 tokens, prepay; activation window to be agreed on signature
- Term: nominal 28-day voucher validity; language will allow a 4-week calendar window (start date inclusive, end date at midnight of day 28) to match procurement preference
- Invoice lines: split into two line items — (1) Voucher (consumable tokens), (2) Implementation credit (one-time service line) — both invoiceable for PO processing
- Concurrency buffer: temporary soft capacity reserve — baseline 6 sustained concurrent slots + 20 burst capacity; documented in runbook and routing notes (not a formal SLA)
- Conversion incentive: if NeuroNova signs an annual commitment within 60 days, we apply voucher value as a credit at 120% toward the annual contract
- Price: one-time charge = $120 (voucher) + $750 implementation credit (example invoice)

Attachments: POC-voucher-agreement.docx (one-page amendment) and we’ll send DocuSign link once you confirm signature party and billing details.

Next steps: please reply with the name and title to sign, the PO number (if you have one), and preferred start date window. We’ll route the DocuSign and schedule a short SRE handoff (15–30m) to document the concurrency buffer.

Thanks — small note: Monica will be your implementation lead for the handoff. Monica, can you propose two 30-minute slots for next week?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
